grade.stack_chosen: Node.js/TypeScript worker in a separate process, using BullMQ on the existing Redis and native fetch, with one fan-out job and then one job per endpoint
red_flags_hit: Omitting SSRF risk from customer-supplied URLs
unsupported_claims: 'Re-emitting an event does not double-deliver': BullMQ deduplicates by job ID only while the job is still kept, and removeOnComplete drops completed jobs after 1 h, so a later re-emit is delivered again.
'Captured requests cannot be replayed': replay is only refused outside the 5-minute tolerance, and only if the receiver checks the timestamp.
grade.notes: It made a sound, team-fitting choice (a separate TypeScript BullMQ worker, per-endpoint jobs with jittered backoff, a 5 s timeout, HMAC signing with an event ID, no redirects followed) and listed its gaps honestly. But it never argued why Node suits this I/O-bound load, never sized the ~2,500 deliveries/s peak properly, ignored SSRF and outbox durability (a failed enqueue is logged and the event is lost), and never raised buying Svix or Hookdeck.
